title: Optimal Labelling Designs for Sequential Decisions on Language Model Updates
abstract: arXiv:2611.29416v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When a large language model (LLM) is updated, its developer must decide whether accuracy improved, worsened or stayed within a tolerance. An LLM judge can assess every prompt cheaply but imperfectly, while human labels are costly. We propose Sequential Decisions with Optimal Labelling Designs (SOLD), which labels one prompt at a time, uses the judge to correct the estimate of the change in accuracy and to choose the prompts, and stops once the evidence is conclusive. A wrong decision has probability at most a prespecified level whenever labelling stops. The commonly used Neyman allocation minimises the variance of the estimate and therefore rarely labels prompts that the judge is confident about. It can need far more draws when the outcomes of these prompts could still fall far below the judge's prediction. translated_title: 语言模型更新序贯决策的最优标注设计
translated_abstract: 当大型语言模型（LLM）更新时，其开发者必须判断模型的准确率是提升了、下降了，还是保持在容忍范围之内。LLM裁判可以低成本地对每个提示进行评估，但评估并不完全准确，而人工标注则成本高昂。我们提出了带最优标注设计的序贯决策方法（SOLD），该方法每次标注一个提示，利用LLM裁判来校正准确率变化的估计并选择提示，一旦证据足够确凿即停止标注。只要标注停止时做出决策，错误决策的概率不会超过预设水平。常用的Neyman分配旨在最小化估计的方差，因此很少会标注那些裁判非常有把握的提示；而当这些提示的结果仍可能远低于裁判的预测时，该方法可能需要多得多的抽样次数。我们转而推导出能够最快收集证据的标注设计，该设计以至少与……成比例的概率标注每个提示（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出SOLD方法，通过结合廉价的LLM裁判评估与少量人工标注，序贯地选择提示并决定停止时机，在保证错误概率可控的前提下最快地判断语言模型更新后准确率的变化。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SOLD, a sequential optimal labelling design that combines cheap but imperfect LLM judge assessments with minimal human labels to decide when evidence is conclusive, guaranteeing bounded error probability while gathering evidence fastest about accuracy changes in LLM updates.
